html:
The Chola conquest of Anuradhapura was the invasion of Sri Lanka by the south Indian Chola Empire, begun by Rajaraja I in 993 and completed by his son Rajendra I in 1017.

The Cholas sacked Anuradhapura, the capital for some 1,400 years, and ruled the north of the island from Polonnaruwa. Rajendra carried the Sinhalese king Mahinda V off to India, where he died.

In 1070 Vijayabahu I drove the Cholas out and kept Polonnaruwa as his capital. Anuradhapura was never the capital again. The new kingdom reached its height under Parakramabahu I. Shiva temples built in the Chola years still stand at Polonnaruwa.
sum: The Chola conquest of Anuradhapura was the invasion of Sri Lanka by the south Indian Chola Empire, begun by Rajaraja I in 993 and completed by his son Rajendra I in 1017.
